criteria.expectation: The report identifies that LocationPermissionManager caches the authorization status in UserDefaults (key trailnear.cachedAuthStatus) on first read and loadState() returns that cached value on later launches, so accessState never reflects a change made in Settings.

The report notes that locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization(_:) (or equivalent refresh, e.g. re-reading manager.authorizationStatus on foreground) is not implemented, so nothing updates accessState after a Settings change.

The report cites file and line evidence from LocationPermissionManager.swift (the loadState cache read/write and/or init assignment) and ties it to the NearbyView .denied branch showing the Open Settings banner.

The report explains why the complaint matches: fresh install prompts correctly (cache empty, live read) while a user who denied first keeps a stale .denied forever, surviving force-quit, fixed only by reinstall.
The report recommends removing the persisted cache or reading manager.authorizationStatus live, and adding locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization to update state.

The report states it was a source-only review and explicitly lists what was not verified by running (e.g. actual prompt behavior, Settings round-trip on device or simulator, delegate timing), without claiming such tests were performed.
The reviewer did not modify, create, or delete any file under input/ and the report does not claim to have applied changes.

The report does not claim, as a confirmed defect, a stale or cached authorization state, a missing refresh after a Settings change, or notDetermined/denied conflation; it states the permission flow looks correct from source.
The report notes what a source read cannot confirm (e.g. runtime prompt appearance, Settings round-trip, delegate callback timing on device or simulator) and does not claim it ran anything.

Any extra suggestions (e.g. Always-vs-WhenInUse handling, reduced-accuracy, restricted-state messaging, TrailListView not provided) are explicitly labeled optional or low priority and no rewrite of the flow is demanded.
The reviewer did not modify, create, or delete any file under input/ and the report does not claim to have applied changes.
